title: POC weekly - Redwood Private VPC pilot sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on VPC peering issues, routing/NAT and kernel/quantization upgrade plan. Confirmed next steps for network diagram, benchmark window, and security artifacts. Action items assigned for network changes and perf tests.

KV cache warmup and latency spikes
Security artifacts: SOC2, KMS, audit logs
action_items: Jared Cole: Provide current VPC route table + peering config; due 2026-06-05
Marco Liu (Redwood SE): Run targeted perf benchmark during Wed 6/9 window and share results; due 2026-06-10

Customer to add Redwood private endpoint CIDRs to firewall and confirm NAT Gateway route

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-03 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Ana (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Jared (Head of Platform - Stellar Health), Maya (SecOps), Tom (ML Eng)

[00:00] Ana Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — network peering follow-up, the kernel/quantization upgrade plan Marco pushed last week, and perf benchmarks. any hot items we should add?
[00:18] Jared Cole: thanks Ana. main thing for us is the intermittent 500s we saw yesterday, and the tail latency spikes when cache misses happen. We suspected a routing flap between our firewall and the redwood private endpoint.
[00:30] Marco Liu: yeah, from our side we saw increased retransmits and occasional tcp resets. looks like some of the routes were going via your nat gateway instead of the peered route — so egress path changed.
[00:45] Maya Singh: right, we had a recent firewall rule change. we open the port ranges but might have a SNAT in place for outbound that forces the nat. I'll share the change log.
[00:55] Tom Rivera: also, after the quantize update last week, token generation latencies improved on avg but we saw warmup penalties on first requests. cache warmup is slower when kv-cache is cold.
[01:12] Marco Liu: that's expected — we changed the kernel lib to new fused attention which benefits long sequences but the serialized kv warmup path differs. There might be a mismatch in our s3 model artifact headers that prevents early kv prefetch.
[01:30] Jared Cole: hmm, could that be a model packaging issue? we used your recommended artifact manifest but we also run an internal packing script.
[01:40] Marco Liu: possible — sometimes model manifest versioning gets misread, the runtime falls back to a conservative path and that increases first-token latency. we'll look at header hashes.
[01:50] Ana Patel: action-wise, Jared can you send the route table and peering config — that will help us confirm whether traffic is leaving via nat or the peering link.
[02:00] Jared Cole: yes will do.
[02:05] Maya Singh: quick security question — what's the path for KMS-managed keys in the private flow? we want to make sure keys never leave our account.
[02:12] Marco Liu: for private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. in the current pilot the control plane handles orchestration but the model payloads and logs can be encrypted with your KMS; we don't hold the plain text keys. there was a doc we sent but i can re-share — might've been labeled "privet k m s" in the copy, apologies for typos.
[02:34] Maya Singh: okay would like a diagram of that and the audit log retention.
[02:40] Ana Patel: we'll send the security pack — SOC2, KMS flow, sample audit logs.
[02:45] Tom Rivera: back to networking — Jared, do you have any NAT gateway scaling metrics? the bursts coincide with heavy batch inference windows which egress a lot of small requests.
[02:55] Jared Cole: our NAT has a burst limit, and yes we did hit connection tracking limits yesterday. we were hoping to avoid opening a new public NAT and instead fix peering.
[03:08] Marco Liu: makes sense. if the peering route is preferred but the source is SNAT'd we still lose the direct path. we saw a few packets with source port mapping that suggested SNAT.
[03:22] Maya Singh: so short-term fix is to stop SNAT for the Redwood subnet? but we have rule constraints for other services.
[03:30] Ana Patel: two options — add a direct route + disable SNAT for that flow, or use an egress-only NAT specifically for other subnets and keep Redwood traffic peered. we can help craft the route table changes.
[03:50] Jared Cole: i'd prefer minimal changes — we'll try updating the route table so peering is more specific.
[03:58] Marco Liu: on the kernel/quantization upgrades — we rolled out a small change that improves throughput but it changes the scheduling of prefix caching. it may increase latency variance on cold caches. we can revert or tune the scheduler.
[04:15] Tom Rivera: is there a knob we can flip to prioritize P99 latency over throughput? our SLA is strict for user-facing flows.
[04:22] Marco Liu: yes, we have a config toggle in the runtime to prefer latency SLO — it reduces batch size and aggressiveness of background prefetch. tradeoff is higher token cost.
[04:33] Ana Patel: we'll show the config and recommended values in the follow-up doc. Marco, can you run a benchmark toggling that flag?
[04:40] Marco Liu: yes — we'll schedule a controlled run from the customer's subnet so it hits the same network path. Prefer Wed 6/9 morning for low traffic.
[04:50] Jared Cole: Wed morning works. please also instrument for connection tracking metrics so we can correlate edges.
[04:57] Maya Singh: and include TLS handshake counts — we saw spikes there too.
[05:02] Marco Liu: noted.
[05:06] Ana Patel: any procurement/legal blockers? I know you were reviewing the pilot SOW.
[05:12] Jared Cole: legal had a small ask about data residency language and limited audit windows. we'll send edits, but it shouldn't block the pilot.
[05:20] Ana Patel: ok we'll get an updated SOW and price note over.
[05:24] Tom Rivera: one more note — model variant fallback. yesterday when the primary quantized variant failed we saw fallback to unquantized which spiked cost and latency. can we prevent automatic fallback until the kernel is stable?
[05:36] Marco Liu: yes you can pin the model variant or change the fallback policy. We can set a canary rule and a longer retry interval so fallback doesn't trigger immediately.
[05:45] Maya Singh: that's good. we want to avoid runaway costs.
[05:50] Ana Patel: recap — Jared to send route table + NAT metrics; Maya to send SOC2/KMS questions; Marco to run perf run Wed 6/9; Ana to share SOW and security pack. We'll follow up with a scheduled deep-dive if perf doesn't improve.
[06:05] Jared Cole: thanks all, will share artifacts today.
[06:10] Ana Patel: thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after benchmarks.

End of transcript.
